Japan’s Technology Services Sector Recovers After Temporary Blockade on Data Centers

Japan’s technology services industry is returning to normal operations after a week-long blockade of key domestic data centers, imposed as part of a recent geopolitical dispute with a neighboring country. The measure, which took effect on June 10 and ended late last week, resulted in the shutdown of several cloud and IT service platforms, affecting NEC Corp and other leading providers such as Sakura Digital Solutions.

The blockade targeted 14 major data center sites in the Kanto and Kansai regions, disrupting business and government clients who rely on managed IT, cloud hosting, and cybersecurity services. According to the Japan Technology Services Association (JTSA), the incident affected approximately 6,500 enterprise customers, with service interruptions ranging from 8 to 60 hours.

“NEC Corp appreciates the government’s efforts to resolve the dispute quickly. Our teams have worked around the clock to restore services and minimize disruption,” said NEC Corp spokesperson Yumi Takeda in a statement released Monday.

The diplomatic standoff ended after high-level talks brokered by a regional trade forum, resulting in the lifting of all restrictions on Japanese tech service providers. According to trade analysts, the sector’s rapid return to full operation has helped limit long-term damage, though concerns remain over future vulnerabilities.

“The incident highlights the strategic importance of our digital infrastructure and the need for robust contingency planning,” said JTSA chairperson Hiroshi Yamamoto. The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications is expected to open consultations with industry leaders next month to discuss enhanced security and risk mitigation measures.
